amendments.reason: The dry run predates behaviour files. Content identities are unaffected (they cover content materials only), so the expected contentSha256 values stand; no behaviourSha256 is predicted and none is compared.

The dry run moved the 18 client adapters and pointers to Core and the 27 Matt copies out of the default. Release 1.7 keeps the frozen default unchanged and adds a closing default release with no items whose retired[] gives all 46 a reason: adapters and pointers have no successor and name Core's per-tool delivery; Matt copies name their Extensions items.
Each of the 27 Matt copies in the frozen default is superseded by its Extensions item with match name+sourcePath against the frozen default's exact digest; the dry run found 0 of 27 hash matches.

The dry run kept the project context as one rule. The maintainer split it into three Project basics items, named by samartomar/aih-catalog#137: the router, a guide document; the working rules and the shared block, two rules. Each carries the folder-neutral form of one material of the frozen default's project context, rendered once by the authored context renderer: it names its neighbours by their place in the folder a project chooses, never a folder name, and promises no per-tool adapter notes. Its content identity is therefore predicted from that rendered text at its item-relative path, not from the frozen bytes; each supersedes the project context by split, and the default's project-context retirement names the three.
Per-tool copies that collapse are superseded by hash when their content identity equals the survivor's, otherwise by name and source path; the dry run listed them without a match.
Every collapsed copy is also retired with its replacement, and templates and frameworks become sets, so their ids are retired; the dry run only marked them.
Hook source items fold into their hook items. The hook ids are decided with the framework migrations, so these retirements are pending on those tickets.
The dry run left 10 Superpowers items unmapped. The 9 per-tool plugin bundles and the duplicate skill library are retired with no item successor; upstream plugin routes become nativeRoutes.
The session bootstrap hook gains a one-line rule as its fallback, an item the dry run did not have; samartomar/aih-catalog#144 names it, so one extra rule is admitted by kind.

The dry run's ecc.notices content identity reproduces from no assignment of item-relative paths to the four shipped notice materials, so it cannot be checked. Their bytes are unchanged: the expectation predicts the identity from those four material digests at the item-relative paths every other ECC item uses, its install target without the .aihq/ecc/ and source/ prefixes (LICENSE, AGENTS.md, plugin.json, README.md).

Each MCP survivor records whether its shipped definition is identical to upstream or edited; an edit is digested as SHA-256 of the canonical JSON {from: upstream, to: shipped} plus LF, in upstream's own encoding.
